AltS qoddomun 'to borrow' < PPh *hedam shows 'the loss of *h, its o reflex of *e, and gemination of the consonant following *e' (p. 454 n. 12); also qolop 'cloud' < *qulep, dalmot 'heavy' < *daRmet (Table 1).
The consonant after *e is geminated: qoddomun < *hedam (n. 12), susbo 'boil' < *sebu, tedokbum < *tidug.
Table 12, 'the most common reflex': *qaRtaq > arta 'man', *qeRes > ares 'worm', *kaRat > arat 'bite', *takaRang > tarang 'rib'. Elsewhere in Luzon only Ilokano has r < *R (p. 464).
Table 13: *baRat > bagat 'banana', *uleR > ulag 'snake', *liqeR > lig 'neck'. g is the reflex of all the Northern Cordilleran languages; Reid takes these words to be loans from them (p. 464).
Table 14, the main reflex: *qujing > quding 'charcoal', *qapeju > apdu 'gall', *pusej > pusəd 'navel', *palaj > palad 'palm'.
'Only two forms show g and these are both probably borrowings from Ilokano' (p. 464).

Table 15, at least 20 forms: *kutu > utu 'louse', *ikan > iyan 'fish', *manuk > manu 'bird', *takaRang > tarang 'rib'. 'This is the only Philippine language which, to my knowledge, lost *k'; words with k are mostly loans from Northern Cordilleran or Ilokano (p. 466). The loss reshaped the pronouns (Tables 16-17).
'A large proportion of these forms give evidence of having been borrowed from a Northern Cordilleran language, or from Ilokano' (p. 466).
'Glottal stop was also lost in words inherited from the proto-language, resulting in the reduction of several vowel sequences to single vowels' (p. 466).

Table 18: vowel harmony after the voiced stops b, d, g: 'if the final vowel of the root was u, the penultimate vowel also became u': *babuy > bubuy 'pig', *ba:lu > bulu 'widow', *dapuR > dupug 'dust', dupuran 'hearth'.
